subject: Biology
title: The Invisible Majority
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Invisible Majority.

hook.text: There are more microbes on Earth than stars in the observable universe.

buildup.text: Microorganisms include bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protists—most invisible to the naked eye.

discovery.text: A single teaspoon of soil contains billions of microbes from thousands of different species.

twist.text: Most microbes are harmless or helpful. Only a small fraction cause disease.

climax.text: Without microbes, dead things wouldn't decay, nutrients wouldn't cycle, and plants couldn't grow.

punchline.text: The tiniest organisms run the planet.

details.summary: Microbes make up the majority of life on Earth by biomass, diversity, and metabolic impact. An estimated trillion microbial species inhabit every environment from deep rock to upper atmosphere, conducting the biogeochemical cycles that make Earth habitable for all other life.
details.whyItMatters: We live in a microbial world. Microbes run the planet's chemistry, cycling carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen. Without them, decomposition would stop, nutrients would be locked away, and complex life would quickly become impossible.
takeaways: Microbial biomass exceeds that of all animals on Earth combined
An estimated trillion microbial species exist, with 99.999 percent undiscovered
Microbes perform essential roles in every major biogeochemical cycle

faq.question: How many microbes are there on Earth?
faq.answer: Estimates suggest approximately one trillion microbial species exist, with 99.999 percent still unknown. The total number of individual microbial cells is estimated at 10 to the 30th power. They inhabit every environment from ocean trenches to the stratosphere.

faq.question: Could complex life exist without microbes?
faq.answer: Almost certainly not. Microbes fix nitrogen for plants, decompose organic matter releasing nutrients, produce oxygen through photosynthesis, and run the carbon and sulfur cycles. They are the invisible infrastructure making Earth habitable for everything else.
